source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 985 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 985 was established by Ordinance No. 30425, passed by the Dallas City Council on April 12, 2017. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 985 is established on property located at the northwest corner of Abrams Road and Northwest Highway. The size of PD 985 is approximately 14.552 acres. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district:

(1) BAIL BOND OFFICE means an office for the issuance, brokerage, or procurement of bail bonds as a main use or an accessory use.

(2) REAR FACADE WALL means a facade wall containing service areas.

(3) SERVICE AREA means any area for loading docks, outdoor storage (other than outdoor display, sales, and storage area), trash collection or compaction, truck parking, or similar functions.

(4) STOOP means a small porch leading to the entrance of a residence.

(5) TATTOO OR BODY PIERCING STUDIO means a business in which tattooing or body piercing is performed. TATTOOING means the practice of producing an indelible mark or figure on the human body by scarring or inserting a pigment under the skin using needles, scalpels, or other related equipment. BODY PIERCING means the piercing of body parts, other than ears, to allow the insertion of jewelry.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a nonresidential zoning district. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Exhibits
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.104. EXHIBITS.

The following exhibits are incorporated into this article:

(1) Exhibit 985A: conceptual plan.

(2) Exhibit 985B: monument sign exhibit. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Conceptual Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.105. CONCEPTUAL PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the conceptual plan (Exhibit 985A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the conceptual plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.106. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

A development plan must be approved by the city plan commission before the issuance of any building permit to authorize work in this district. If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.107. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

(a) Except as provided in this section, the only main uses permitted are those main uses permitted in the RR Regional Retail District, subject to the same conditions applicable in the RR Regional Retail District, as set out in Chapter 51A. For example, a use permitted in the RR Regional Retail District only by specific use permit (SUP) is permitted in this district only by SUP; a use subject to development impact review (DIR) in the RR Regional Retail District is subject to DIR in this district; etc.

(b) The following uses are prohibited:

-- Alternative financial establishment. -- Bail bond office. -- Building repair and maintenance shop. -- Commercial amusement (outside). -- Gas drilling and production. -- Halfway house. -- Overnight general purpose shelter. -- Swap or buy shop. -- Tattoo or body piercing studio. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.108. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.109. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) Setbacks.

(1) Applicability. Setbacks apply to the perimeter of the Property only. Setbacks are not required between lots within the Property.

(2) Minimum setbacks. Except as provided in this subsection, minimum setback is:

(A) 20 feet along Abrams Road.

(B) 20 feet along Northwest Highway.

(C) 20 feet along Theater Way/northern boundary.

(D) 10 feet along all other perimeter property lines.

(3) Urban form setback and tower spacing. An additional 20-foot front yard setback is required for that portion of a structure above 45 feet in height along Northwest Highway and along Abrams Road. An additional setback of 10 feet is required for any portion of a structure above 45 feet in height along Theater Way or other perimeter property lines. No additional setbacks for structures greater than 45 feet are required for internal lot lines.

(4) Projections. Balconies, bay windows, awnings, eaves, patios, signs, and entryways affixed to the building or part of the foundation may project up to five feet into a required setback. Stoops, retaining walls, benches, pots, raised planters, sculptures, cabanas, and other decorative landscape items may be located within the required setback.

(b) Density. No maximum density.

(c) Floor area ratio.

(1) Maximum floor area ratio for the entire Property is 2:1. Maximum floor area ratio for any individual lot is 4:1.

(2) The maximum floor area for non-residential uses is 500,000 square feet. No maximum floor area for residential uses.

(d) Height.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, maximum structure height is 54 feet.

(2) For parking structures, maximum structure height is 60 feet.

(3) Roof-mounted mechanical equipment may project up to eight feet above the maximum structure height.

(4) No non-residential structures with a height greater than 45 feet are allowed within 100 feet of the northern boundary of the property.

(5) If any portion of a structure is over 26 feet in height, that portion may not be located above a residential proximity slope. Chimneys may project through the slope to a height 12 feet above the slope and 12 feet above the maximum height. The following structures may project through the slope to a height not to exceed the maximum structure height, or 12 feet above the slope, whichever is less:

(A) Elevator penthouse or bulkhead.

(B) Mechanical equipment room.

(C) Cooling tower.

(D) Tank designed to hold liquids.

(E) Ornamental cupola or dome.

(F) Skylights.

(G) Clerestory.

(H) Visual screens that surround roof mounted mechanical equipment.

(I) Vent stacks.

(J) Amateur communications tower.

(K) Parapet wall, limited to a height of four feet.

(e) Lot coverage.

(1) Maximum lot coverage for the entire Property is 70 percent.

(2) Maximum lot coverage for any individual lot is 80 percent.

(3) Aboveground parking structures are included in lot coverage calculations; surface parking lots and underground parking structures are not.

(f) Lot size. No minimum lot size.

(g) Stories.

(1) Except as provided in this subsection, no minimum or maximum number of stories.

(2) For parking structures, maximum number of stories above grade is five. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.110. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, consult the use regulations in Division 51A- 4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use.

(b) Except as provided in this subsection, for uses housed in one contiguous structure with a total floor area greater than 100,000 square feet, one space per 250 square feet of floor area is required. If the floor area for all restaurant and alcoholic beverage establishment uses combined exceeds 12,500 square feet in a contiguous structure with a floor area greater than 100,000 square feet, the floor area of restaurant and alcoholic beverage establishment uses exceeding 12,500 square feet must be parked at one space per 125 square feet of floor area.

(c) Parking lots must have a pedestrian pathway system distinguished from the parking and driving surface by landscape barriers or a change in surface materials such as pavers or patterned concrete. Pedestrian pathways may not be distinguished by paint alone. Pedestrian pathways must be a minimum of six feet wide. There must be a minimum of one pedestrian pathway into the Property from Northwest Highway and from Abrams Road.

(d) Parking lots, excluding spaces adjacent to the perimeter of the Property, must be divided into sections containing no more than 200 parking spaces. Parking lots must be divided by landscaped dividers. Landscaped dividers must have trees spaced at a maximum of 40 feet on center and ground cover or shrubs. Pedestrian pathways with a minimum of five feet must be provided as a means of dividing the parking lot.

(e) For parking and loading purposes the entire Property is considered one lot. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.111. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition.

(c) Minimum widths for landscape buffers are:

(1) 10 feet along Abrams Road;

(2) 10 feet along Theater Way/northern boundary;

(3) five feet along the western boundary of the Property; and

(4) 10 feet along Northwest Highway.

(d) Landscaped islands of a minimum of 80 square feet per row of cars must be placed at both ends of each parking row. Each landscaped island must have ground cover and a minimum of one tree.

(e) Except as provided in this subsection, perimeter landscape buffer strips along Theater Way and the northern and western boundaries of the Property must contain large trees spaced no farther than 40 feet on center. Designated buffer plant materials are not required within any required perimeter landscape buffer strip where a local utility easement and installation prohibits the planting and maintenance of trees or shrubs. A sidewalk may be placed between the northern Property boundary and the perimeter landscape buffer strip. The required perimeter landscape buffer strip along Northwest Highway and Abrams Road must be landscaped with a minimum three-foot-tall evergreen hedge and large trees spaced at a maximum 40 feet on center. Article X mandatory landscape buffers and screening of off-street parking may be counted as design standards.

(f) All mandatory landscape buffers must be installed prior to the initial certificate of occupancy for any use on the Property.

(g) Site, street trees, and parking lot trees must have a minimum caliper of three inches.

(h) No required parking space may be located more than 80 feet from the trunk of a large canopy tree.

(i) If the Property is developed with nonresidential uses, a minimum of five percent of the Property must be designated as landscaped area. Landscaping may include ground cover, turf grass, seasonal plantings, trees, or shrubs. The required landscaped area may include landscaped medians and buffers. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.113. SIGNS.

(a) Except as provided in this section, signs must comply with the provisions for business zoning districts in Article VII.

(b) For purposes of non-premise signs and movement control signs, the Property is considered one lot.

(c) One multi-tenant monument sign is allowed along Northwest Highway. This sign may not exceed 35 feet in height or have a maximum effective area greater than 450 square feet as shown on the monument sign exhibit (Exhibit 985B). This sign must be set back a minimum of 20 feet from Northwest Highway.

(d) One multi-tenant monument sign is allowed along Abrams Road. This sign may not exceed 35 feet in height or have a maximum effective area greater than 375 square feet as shown on the monument sign exhibit. This sign must be set back a minimum of 10 feet from Abrams Road.

(e) Movement control signs for a hospital or a medical clinic or ambulatory surgical center use and must meet the following requirements:

(1) Maximum effective area is six square feet.

(2) Characters on the sign may not exceed eight inches in height. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Design Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.114. DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) No more than 75 percent of a facade wall, exclusive of fenestration, may have a single material or color.

(b) Vinyl siding may not be used as an exterior finish. Metal siding may be used on up to 15 percent of each facade.

(c) Except as provided in this subsection, facades must incorporate:

(1) Changes of color, texture, or material, either diagonally or vertically, at intervals of not less than 30 feet and not more than 100 feet.

(2) Changes in plane with a depth of at least four inches, horizontally or vertically, at intervals of not less than 30 feet and not more than 100 feet.

(d) Rear facade walls must be made up of two or more of the following materials: concrete, stone, brick, stucco, or masonry units.

(e) Rear facade walls must incorporate at least two of the following design elements:

(1) A repeating pattern of wall recesses and projections, such as bays, offsets, reveals, or projecting ribs, that have a relief of at least four inches.

(2) A repeating pattern of pilasters projecting from the facade wall by a minimum of four inches.

(3) Trim or accent elements using decorative contrasting colors.

(4) Trim or accent elements using decorative colors of at least 10 percent of the area of the facade wall exclusive of fenestration.

(f) Split faced or smooth faced concrete block and tilt-up concrete panels that are textured and painted may only be used on rear facade walls.

(g) Facades facing Northwest Highway or Abrams Road must incorporate one or more of the following:

(1) Changes of color, texture, or material, either diagonally, horizontally, or vertically, at intervals of not less 20 feet and not more than 200 feet.

(2) Changes in plane with a depth of at least eight inches, either diagonally, horizontally, or vertically, at intervals of not less than 20 feet and not more than 200 feet.

(h) Shopping cart storage areas adjacent to facades (not located in parking lots) must be screened with landscaping or a maximum four-foot-high wall constructed of materials matching the materials of the primary facade. No more than two shopping cart storage areas, one on each side of an entrance, may be provided on any facade. Shopping cart storage areas may not exceed 40 feet in length. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Sidewalks
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.115. SIDEWALKS.

(a) In addition to the pedestrian pathway system required for parking lots in Section 51P-985.110, all buildings are required to have an unobstructed four-foot-wide sidewalk around the perimeter. This provision does not apply to rear facade walls.

(b) Sidewalks along Abrams Road must have a minimum unobstructed width of six feet.

(c) Sidewalks are not required along Northwest Highway. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.116. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Upon the issuance of certificates of occupancy for 125,000 square feet of floor area, no additional building permits, except for grading or utility permits, may be issued until a traffic control light is installed at the corner of Northwest Highway and abandoned Quality Lane, subject to Texas Department of Transportation approval.

(b) A maximum of two drive-in or drive-through uses are allowed on the Property.

(c) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(d) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 30425)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-985.117. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 30425)
